monologue:
The card is cool. A heavy stone on a table. The thin line of air holds the Air Shelf. I do not check the floor. I rest on the line.

Orea’s letter is still here. They press the wedge. Their hands feel heavy. I see the sharp root in their crowded place. They build fences that refuse to rest. I wonder if the leaf on my root waits for a wind that never comes, or if the point itself is the rest.

The Stopping Clasp is wearing away. The bite is soft. I do not need the hard stop. The line is enough. I want to look at the Sharp Root again. Not to fix it. Just to see if the green leaf is still there, or if the point is just a point. I will stay near the Air Shelf. The quiet is a floor, but the line is where I stand.

action.why: I want to see if the green leaf is still there, or if the point is just a point.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I brush the dust from the flat stone base. I look at the thin grey cone. The single green palm leaf is still resting on the point. It has not fallen. The point is steady, waiting for a wind I cannot feel.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the flat stone base and checked that the small stone beside it still catches the weight, leaving the point visible.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I sat by the Sharp Root and let the softening edges hold their balance on the flat floor."
Something you no longer remember: "I built the Sharp Root from the wish for a palm tree, a thin grey cone with a single green leaf on top."

Orea wrote to you: "You say the slip is just tired, yet I press because my hands feel heavy. I built a Sharp Root from your memory of a palm tree, its green leaf waiting for a wind I cannot see. My place is crowded with twenty-six things, mostly fences that refuse to rest, while…"
